This was my first ever PC build, and I haven't looked into parts since I built this last June, but from info I have on hand and from what I can remember:

  • i5-4460. Intel seems better than AMD in the CPU game, I can't remember the reasons, but something about them being more powerful overall. Like, what Intel needs 4 cores for, AMD has 6. That sort of thinking.
  • Some cheap motherboard that cost me £30. I really, really wish I understood how motherboards worked better when I was building. For example, everything fits (literally only just, its quite a small motherboard), but I should've got a bigger one because a) my hands are pretty big, and b) there's not enough fan power slots. I have 3 fans (2 intake on the front, 1 exhaust on the back), but only 1 intake is working because there's not enough slots on the motherboard for me to add the second one on the front. My GPU covered the PCIe slot I was going to use for a wireless adapter, so I had to buy a USB one instead, the very thing I wanted to avoid.
  • 8GB Kingston HyperX RAM. From what I could tell, and still can, 8GB seems to be the current sweet spot for RAM. 4GB is just about scraping it but newer games are wanting 6GB RAM. Also, it's better to have more than you need than not enough. 16GB seemed overkill though, considering I'm just gaming on this.
  • My graphics card; the PowerColor PCS+ R9 290. I watched a video comparing the 970 and 290, and whilst the performance was virtually the same, the 290 actually had the 4GB VRAM, whereas the 970 had some stuttering once it hit 3.5GB. I also didn't think their business practise was very great in this regard, so I opted for the 290. The PCS+ was the best of them all, so that's why I chose it.
  • A 1TB Western Digital HDD for my shit, and a 240GB OCZ SSD for my OS (Windows 8.1, now Windows 10), the majority of my programs (browsers, etc) and GTA V (I've spent my fair share waiting when I had it on PS3). I really need to spend some time and sift through what I have on my HDD, because I feel it's filled up way too quickly - that could be because I have a lot of shit, and it probably is, but I still need to go through it and uninstall games I don't play, software I don't use anymore, etc. I'm not too fussed about using Windows 10 - I don't do much more on here than gaming except for some online buying, emails, and some work, so at least MS can see I have decent taste in games. I've also got an overflow 500GB Seagate HDD, but that was
  • I've also got a DVD drive, because my copy of Windows 8.1 came by disc, I didn't have a laptop to take it from etc.
  • My case is a Corsair Carbide SPEC-03 (how can you forget that name!) and it's literally just big enough. Pretty robust, and I can easily reach the side to feel the temperature, which I can then decide if it's hot enough to actually check in Speccy or if I'm okay (that lukewarm warm feeling).
  • Finally, my PSU is a EVGA 750W. It was recommended by multiple people. The price difference between it and the 600W one I was going to buy was negligible, and it's of much better quality. Also, 750W is what the R9 290 wants as a recommendation.
  • Monitor is just a 32" Full HD TV, and the keyboard and muse s just a cheap double pack I picked up from a PC store.

I built it over a couple days. I wanted to take my time and not rush it and fail. I made a couple mistakes along the way, but nothing detrimental to the intergrity of the PC.

I won't dive into budget, but I went over what I wanted to spend, and should've taken a bit more consideration.

If I had to upgrade, I'd want a bigger case (my hands are giant and I like space to work in), a bigger motherboard (to the GPU isn't covering half of it and just more space and choice for things). I'm not sure how long my 290 will last me, but it's tackled everything I play pretty well, and delivered some very gorgeous experiences. I don't regret going full PC, although in hindsight, there's a couple of things I'd have done differently. Maybe next time.
